source.text: Παῦλος δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς Φιλήμονι τῷ ἀγαπητῷ καὶ συνεργῷ ἡμῶν καὶ Ἀπφίᾳ τῇ ἀδελφῇ καὶ Ἀρχίππῳ τῷ συστρατιώτῃ ἡμῶν καὶ τῇ κατ’ οἶκόν σου ἐκκλησίᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: Paul, prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon the beloved and fellow worker of us, \v 2 and to Apphia the sister and to Archippus the fellow soldier of us and to the at house of you church;

en.L: Paul, a prisoner of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, and Timothy [our] brother, to Philemon our beloved [friend] and fellow worker, \v 2 and to Apphia [our] sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house.
en.B: From Paul, a prisoner for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and from Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our dear friend and fellow worker, \v 2 to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your home.
en.R: This letter is from Paul, who is in prison because of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and from our brother Timothy. We are writing to Philemon, our dear friend who works with us. \v 2 We are also writing to our sister Apphia, to Archippus, who fights beside us like a soldier, and to the church that meets in your home, Philemon.

fr.L: Paul, prisonnier du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, et Timothée [notre] frère, à Philémon notre bien-aimé et collaborateur, \v 2 et à Apphia [notre] sœur, et à Archippe notre compagnon d’armes, et à l’église [qui est] dans ta maison.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, prisonnier pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, et de Timothée notre frère, à Philémon, notre cher ami et collaborateur, \v 2 à Apphia notre sœur, à Archippe notre compagnon d’armes, et à l’église qui se réunit dans ta maison.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul, qui est en prison à cause du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, et de notre frère Timothée. Nous écrivons à Philémon, notre cher ami qui travaille avec nous. \v 2 Nous écrivons aussi à notre sœur Apphia, à Archippe, qui combat à nos côtés comme un soldat, et à l’église qui se réunit chez toi, Philémon.

decisions.choice: a prisoner of Christ Jesus: in prison because of Christ, and belonging to him
alternatives: a prisoner in a figurative sense only
decisions.reason: Paul is really in custody (verses 9, 10, 13, 23). In most of his letters he opens with "apostle"; here he writes as a prisoner and a friend, because he means to appeal rather than command (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: Philemon: a believer in Colossae, a householder who owned slaves
decisions.reason: Onesimus and Archippus belong to Colossae (Colossians 4:9, 4:17), so Philemon most likely lived there. His house was large enough for the church to meet in, and he had become a believer through Paul (verse 19).

decisions.choice: Apphia: a woman of the household church
decisions.reason: "Sister" means a fellow believer. Because she is named next to Philemon, she is often thought to be his wife, but the letter does not say so.

decisions.choice: fellow soldier: a comrade in the work of the gospel
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same word of Epaphroditus (Philippians 2:25). Archippus has a task from the Lord to carry out (Colossians 4:17).

decisions.choice: your house: Philemon's
decisions.reason: σου is singular. The letter is addressed to Philemon ("you" is singular through verse 21, except in verses 3 and 22), but the church in his house hears it too.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: a prisoner for the sake of (B); in prison because of (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why Paul is a prisoner (m1).

decisions.choice: our dear friend
decisions.reason: "Beloved" used alone is no longer everyday English.

decisions.choice: your home, Philemon
decisions.reason: Readable names Philemon so that "your" is clear after a list of names (m5).

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}"; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: the title needs an article in French and "en" does not take one, so the span for "in Christ" covers the preposition (verses 8, 20, 23). Elsewhere the article stays outside the span. "Jesus Christ" is "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: l’église, lowercase, for the congregation that meets in Philemon's house (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French keeps the capital for the whole body of believers; one local gathering is "l’église", as in Colossians 4:15.

source.text: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will show you grace and give you peace.

fr.L: Grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Je prie pour que Dieu notre Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous accordent leur grâce et leur paix.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the whole household church
decisions.reason: ὑμῖν is plural: the greeting is for everyone named in verses 1-2.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as Philippians 1:2 and Colossians 1:2 do.

decisions.choice: "vous" where the Greek you is plural (verses 3, 22, 25); "tu" to Philemon everywhere else (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French can show what English cannot: the greeting, the prayers of verse 22 and the closing blessing are for the whole household church (m1), while the appeal itself is to Philemon alone.

source.text: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου πάντοτε μνείαν σου ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, ἀκούων σου τὴν ἀγάπην καὶ τὴν πίστιν ἣν ἔχεις πρὸς τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους, ὅπως ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου ἐνεργὴς γένηται ἐν ἐπιγνώσει παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ τοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν εἰς Χριστόν·

records.literal_gloss: I thank the God of me always, mention of you making in the prayers of me, \v 5 hearing of you the love and the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the holy [ones], \v 6 so that the sharing of the faith of you effective may become in knowledge of every good [thing] the [one] in us for Christ;

en.L: I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers, \v 5 because I hear of your love and of the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the holy ones, \v 6 [and I pray] that the sharing of your faith may become effective in [the] knowledge of every good thing that is in us for {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Whenever I remember you in my prayers, I always thank my God, \v 5 because I keep hearing about your love for all God's holy people and your faith in the Lord Jesus. \v 6 I pray that the generosity that flows from your faith will be put to work, as you come to know fully all the good that is ours, for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: I always thank my God when I pray for you. \v 5 I keep hearing about how much you love all of God's people, and about your faith in the Lord Jesus. \v 6 I pray that your faith, which makes you share so generously with others, will do even more good. And I pray that you will come to know fully all the good things God has given us to live for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Je rends grâce à mon Dieu toujours, faisant mention de toi dans mes prières, \v 5 parce que j’entends parler de ton amour et de la foi que tu as envers le Seigneur Jésus et pour tous les saints, \v 6 [et je prie] pour que la communion de ta foi devienne efficace dans la connaissance de tout bien qui [est] en nous pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Chaque fois que je me souviens de toi dans mes prières, je remercie toujours mon Dieu, \v 5 car j’entends sans cesse parler de ton amour pour tout le peuple saint de Dieu et de ta foi dans le Seigneur Jésus. \v 6 Je prie pour que la générosité qui naît de ta foi porte tout son effet, à mesure que tu connais pleinement tout le bien qui est à nous, pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Je remercie toujours mon Dieu quand je prie pour toi. \v 5 J’entends sans cesse parler de ton grand amour pour tout le peuple de Dieu, et de ta foi dans le Seigneur Jésus. \v 6 Ta foi te pousse à partager généreusement avec les autres, et je prie pour que cela fasse encore plus de bien. Je prie aussi pour que tu connaisses pleinement toutes les bonnes choses que Dieu nous a données pour que nous vivions pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: "always" goes with giving thanks: every time he prays for Philemon
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:3, the thanks rises whenever Paul remembers him in prayer.

decisions.choice: love for all the holy ones, and faith in the Lord Jesus: a crossed order
alternatives: both love and faith directed to both the Lord and his people
decisions.reason: Paul names love, then faith, then the Lord, then the holy ones: faith goes with the Lord and love with his people, as in Colossians 1:4 ("your faith in Christ Jesus and the love you have for all the holy ones"). Verse 7 picks up his love for God's people.

decisions.choice: the sharing that comes from your faith: Philemon's generous fellowship with other believers, which Paul prays will have full effect
alternatives: sharing your faith with others: telling them the gospel
your share in the faith that all believers hold in common
decisions.reason: ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου can mean several things. κοινωνία is sharing or partnership, often generosity to others (Romans 15:26; 2 Corinthians 9:13). Verse 7 praises Philemon for refreshing God's people, and verses 17-20 will ask for the same kind of partnership toward Onesimus, so Paul probably prays that Philemon's faith-born sharing will work powerfully. The verse is among the hardest in Paul's letters, and none of the readings can be ruled out.

decisions.choice: knowledge: full, personal knowledge
decisions.reason: ἐπιγνώσει is the word for real knowledge used in Colossians 1:9-10.

decisions.choice: for Christ: for his sake, leading toward him
decisions.reason: εἰς Χριστόν means toward or for Christ: the good believers have is given so that they live for him.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in us"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "in you" (plural). The two Greek words differ by one letter. The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: your love for all God's holy people and your faith in the Lord Jesus
alternatives: your love and the faith you have toward the Lord Jesus and all the holy ones
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable pair each with its object (m2).

decisions.choice: the generosity that flows from your faith
decisions.reason: Balanced states the sense chosen in m3, which is uncertain; Literal keeps "sharing".

decisions.choice: your faith, which makes you share so generously with others, will do even more good; all the good things God has given us to live for Christ
alternatives: the sharing of your faith may become effective in the knowledge of every good thing in us for Christ
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the sense chosen in m3 and m5.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu, le peuple de Dieu (B, R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As Colossians: "les saints" today suggests canonised individuals, so Balanced and Readable say who is meant, all God's people.

decisions.choice: la communion de ta foi (L)
decisions.reason: "Le partage de ta foi" would be read as telling others about the faith; the sense chosen in m3 is the fellowship and generosity that come from it, which "communion" keeps open at Literal while Balanced and Readable state it.

source.text: χαρὰν γὰρ πολλὴν ἔσχον καὶ παράκλησιν ἐπὶ τῇ ἀγάπῃ σου, ὅτι τὰ σπλάγχνα τῶν ἁγίων ἀναπέπαυται διὰ σοῦ, ἀδελφέ.

records.literal_gloss: Joy for much I had and encouragement over the love of you, because the hearts of the holy [ones] have been refreshed through you, brother.

en.L: For I had much joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the holy ones have been refreshed through you, brother.
en.B: Brother, your love has filled me with joy and encouragement, because through you God's holy people have been refreshed at heart.
en.R: Brother, your love has given me great joy and has encouraged me. You have cheered up God's people and given them new strength.

fr.L: Car j’ai eu beaucoup de joie et d’encouragement grâce à ton amour, parce que les cœurs des saints ont été soulagés par toi, frère.
fr.B: Frère, ton amour m’a rempli de joie et d’encouragement, car grâce à toi le cœur du peuple saint de Dieu a été réconforté.
fr.R: Frère, ton amour m’a donné une grande joie et m’a encouragé. Tu as remonté le moral du peuple de Dieu et tu lui as redonné des forces.

decisions.choice: the hearts: the inner self, where feeling lives
decisions.reason: σπλάγχνα means the inner organs, thought of as the seat of feeling (Colossians 3:12). It is a key word of this letter: Onesimus is Paul's "heart" (verse 12), and Paul asks Philemon to refresh his heart (verse 20) as he has refreshed others.

decisions.choice: refreshed: given rest and relief
decisions.reason: ἀναπαύω means to give rest (Matthew 11:28). The perfect says the refreshment lasts.

decisions.choice: brother: fellow believer, said with affection
decisions.reason: Paul ends the sentence with ἀδελφέ, and uses it again in verse 20 as he makes his request.

decisions.choice: Brother, ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the address first, as is natural in English.

decisions.choice: cheered up God's people and given them new strength
alternatives: the hearts of the holy ones have been refreshed
decisions.reason: Readable says what refreshing the heart means (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Philemon is a letter: Paul speaks to Philemon about what has happened ("j’ai eu beaucoup de joie", "ont été soulagés"), and French uses the passé composé for that, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: soulagés (L); réconforté (B); the same verb in verse 20
decisions.reason: "Rafraîchir le cœur" is not French; the word means given rest and relief (m2), which "soulager" says at Literal and "réconforter" in more natural French at Balanced.

source.text: Διό, πολλὴν ἐν Χριστῷ παρρησίαν ἔχων ἐπιτάσσειν σοι τὸ ἀνῆκον, διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην μᾶλλον παρακαλῶ, τοιοῦτος ὢν ὡς Παῦλος πρεσβύτης νυνὶ δὲ καὶ δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρακαλῶ σε περὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ τέκνου, ὃν ἐγέννησα ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς Ὀνήσιμον, τόν ποτέ σοι ἄχρηστον νυνὶ δὲ σοὶ καὶ ἐμοὶ εὔχρηστον, ὃν ἀνέπεμψά σοι αὐτόν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὰ ἐμὰ σπλάγχνα·

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, much in Christ boldness having to command you the fitting [thing], \v 9 because of the love rather I appeal, such a one being as Paul an old man, now and also a prisoner of Christ Jesus; \v 10 I appeal to you concerning the my child, whom I begot in the chains, Onesimus, \v 11 the [one] once to you useless, now but both to you and to me useful, \v 12 whom I sent back to you, him, that is, the my heart;

en.L: Therefore, though I have much boldness in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to command you what is fitting, \v 9 yet because of love I rather appeal [to you], being such a one as Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus. \v 10 I appeal to you for my child, whom I fathered in [my] chains, Onesimus, \v 11 who once was useless to you but now is useful both to you and to me, \v 12 whom I have sent back to you, him, that is, my very heart.
en.B: So although in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} I could be bold enough to order you to do what you ought, \v 9 I would rather appeal to you on the basis of love. I, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, \v 10 appeal to you for my child Onesimus, who became my son while I was in chains. \v 11 Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful to you and to me. \v 12 I am sending him back to you, and he is my very heart.
en.R: So I could be bold and order you to do what is right, because of my authority in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 9 But because of the love we share, I would rather ask you. I, Paul, am an old man, and now I am also a prisoner because of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 10 I am asking you to help Onesimus. He is like a son to me, because he became a believer through me while I was in prison. \v 11 His name means "useful." Before, he was not useful to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me. \v 12 I am sending him back to you, and sending him is like sending my own heart.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, bien qu’ayant {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} beaucoup d’assurance pour te prescrire ce qui convient, \v 9 c’est plutôt à cause de l’amour que je fais appel [à toi], étant tel que [je suis], Paul, un vieillard, et maintenant aussi prisonnier du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. \v 10 Je fais appel à toi pour mon enfant, que j’ai engendré dans [mes] chaînes, Onésime, \v 11 qui autrefois t’était inutile, mais maintenant [est] utile à toi et à moi, \v 12 que je t’ai renvoyé, lui, c’est-à-dire mon propre cœur.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, bien que j’aie {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} toute l’assurance voulue pour t’ordonner de faire ce que tu dois, \v 9 je préfère faire appel à toi au nom de l’amour. Moi, Paul, un homme âgé, et maintenant aussi prisonnier pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, \v 10 je fais appel à toi pour mon enfant Onésime, qui est devenu mon fils pendant que j’étais dans les chaînes. \v 11 Autrefois, il t’était inutile, mais maintenant il est utile, à toi comme à moi. \v 12 Je te le renvoie, lui qui est mon propre cœur.
fr.R: Je pourrais donc avoir l’audace de t’ordonner de faire ce qui est juste, grâce à l’autorité que j’ai {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}. \v 9 Mais à cause de l’amour qui nous unit, je préfère te le demander. Moi, Paul, je suis un vieil homme, et maintenant je suis aussi en prison à cause du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. \v 10 Je te demande d’aider Onésime. Il est comme un fils pour moi, parce qu’il est devenu croyant grâce à moi quand j’étais en prison. \v 11 Son nom veut dire « utile ». Avant, il ne t’était pas utile, mais maintenant il est utile, à toi comme à moi. \v 12 Je te le renvoie, et c’est comme si je t’envoyais mon propre cœur.

decisions.choice: though I could command, I appeal
decisions.reason: The participle ἔχων ("having") is concessive: Paul has the right in Christ to give orders, but chooses to ask. παρρησίαν is the boldness or freedom of speech that his place in Christ gives him.

decisions.choice: an old man
decisions.reason: πρεσβύτης means an old man (Luke 1:18; Titus 2:2), and Paul would have been in his fifties or sixties. Because a similar word differing by one letter means "ambassador", and Ephesians 6:20 calls Paul "an ambassador in chains", some read that here. No manuscript has it, and "old man" fits Paul's appeal to his age and his chains.

decisions.choice: my child, whom I fathered in chains: Onesimus became a believer through Paul while Paul was in prison
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of those he brought to faith as his children (1 Corinthians 4:15; Galatians 4:19). Onesimus came to faith while Paul was in custody.

decisions.choice: the name comes last
decisions.reason: Paul holds back the name Ὀνήσιμον until the end of the clause, after "my child": Philemon hears who Onesimus now is before he hears his name.

decisions.choice: a play on the name: Onesimus means "useful"
decisions.reason: Ὀνήσιμος means useful or profitable, a common name for slaves. Paul plays on it: once ἄχρηστον ("useless"), now εὔχρηστον ("useful"), to Philemon and to Paul.

decisions.choice: I am sending him back: the past tense of letters, perhaps also "referring his case" to Philemon
decisions.reason: ἀνέπεμψά is written from the time the letter is read, when Onesimus will have arrived with it. The verb can also mean to refer a case to the one who decides it (Acts 25:21).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "him, that is, my very heart"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "receive him" (from verse 17) to complete the sentence. The SBLGNT leaves the sentence as it is.

decisions.choice: my very heart: as dear to Paul as his own self
decisions.reason: See verse 7: σπλάγχνα is the word for the inner self.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: became my son (B); He is like a son to me ... became a believer through me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Paul's "fathering" means (m3).

decisions.choice: His name means "useful."
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay, which is lost in translation (m5).

decisions.choice: I am sending
decisions.reason: The tense natural in English (m6), as in Colossians 4:8.

decisions.choice: because of the love we share
decisions.reason: The love is the love between Paul and Philemon, and the love Philemon shows (verses 5, 7).

decisions.choice: je fais appel à toi (L, B); je te demande (R)
decisions.reason: Paul sets a request made in love against an order he could give (m1). "Exhorter" sounds like preaching, and "je te prie" is weak in modern French; "faire appel à" keeps the earnest appeal.

source.text: ὃν ἐγὼ ἐβουλόμην πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν κατέχειν, ἵνα ὑπὲρ σοῦ μοι διακονῇ ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·

records.literal_gloss: whom I was wishing with myself to keep, so that on behalf of you to me he might serve in the chains of the gospel, \v 14 without but the your consent nothing I wished to do, so that not as by compulsion the good of you may be but by willingness;

en.L: I wanted to keep him with me, so that he might serve me on your behalf in the chains of the gospel, \v 14 but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good [deed] might not be as by compulsion but of [your own] free will.
en.B: I would have liked to keep him here with me, so that he could serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel. \v 14 But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that any good you do would come from your own free choice and not be forced.
en.R: I wanted to keep him here with me. He could help me in your place while I am in prison for telling the good news. \v 14 But I did not want to do anything unless you agreed. I want the good you do to be something you choose to do, not something you are forced to do.

fr.L: Je voulais le garder auprès de moi, afin qu’il me serve à ta place dans les chaînes de l’Évangile, \v 14 mais je n’ai rien voulu faire sans ton consentement, afin que ton bienfait ne soit pas comme par contrainte, mais de [ton plein] gré.
fr.B: J’aurais aimé le garder ici avec moi, pour qu’il me serve à ta place pendant que je suis dans les chaînes pour l’Évangile. \v 14 Mais je n’ai rien voulu faire sans ton accord, pour que le bien que tu feras vienne de ton libre choix et ne soit pas forcé.
fr.R: Je voulais le garder ici avec moi. Il aurait pu m’aider à ta place pendant que je suis en prison pour avoir annoncé la bonne nouvelle. \v 14 Mais je n’ai rien voulu faire sans que tu sois d’accord. Je veux que le bien que tu fais soit un choix de ta part, et non une chose qu’on t’oblige à faire.

decisions.choice: I wanted: a wish Paul did not act on
decisions.reason: The past tense ἐβουλόμην describes what Paul would have liked, set aside out of respect for Philemon's rights.

decisions.choice: on your behalf: in your place
decisions.reason: Philemon would gladly have served Paul himself; Onesimus could do it for him. διακονῇ is the verb of serving used of Christ's servants.

decisions.choice: your good: the kindness Paul hopes Philemon will choose
decisions.reason: Paul does not say what the good deed is. It must be freely chosen, not forced (2 Corinthians 9:7).

decisions.choice: in prison for telling the good news
alternatives: in the chains of the gospel
decisions.reason: Readable says what "chains of the gospel" means.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R) (for the whole letter)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As Colossians: Readable says "good news" because "Évangile" is church language.

source.text: τάχα γὰρ διὰ τοῦτο ἐχωρίσθη πρὸς ὥραν ἵνα αἰώνιον αὐτὸν ἀπέχῃς, οὐκέτι ὡς δοῦλον ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ δοῦλον, ἀδελφὸν ἀγαπητόν, μάλιστα ἐμοί, πόσῳ δὲ μᾶλλον σοὶ καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ ἐν κυρίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps for because of this he was separated for an hour, so that eternally him you might have back, \v 16 no longer as a slave but beyond a slave, a brother beloved, especially to me, how much but more to you, both in flesh and in Lord.

en.L: For perhaps this is why he was separated [from you] for a while, so that you might have him back forever, \v 16 no longer as a slave but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in [the] flesh and in [the] Lord.
en.B: Perhaps this is why he was parted from you for a little while: so that you might have him back for good, \v 16 no longer as a slave but as more than a slave, a dear brother. He is especially dear to me, and how much more to you, both in everyday life and in the Lord.
en.R: Maybe this is why Onesimus was away from you for a short time: so that you could have him back forever. \v 16 But now he is not just a slave. He is much more than a slave. He is a brother whom we love. He means a lot to me, and he should mean even more to you, both as a person in your household and as a brother in the Lord.

fr.L: Car peut-être est-ce pour cela qu’il a été séparé [de toi] pour un moment, afin que tu le retrouves pour toujours, \v 16 non plus comme un esclave, mais plus qu’un esclave, un frère bien-aimé, surtout pour moi, mais combien plus pour toi, et dans la chair et dans le Seigneur.
fr.B: Peut-être est-ce pour cela qu’il a été séparé de toi pour un peu de temps : afin que tu le retrouves pour de bon, \v 16 non plus comme un esclave, mais comme bien plus qu’un esclave, un frère cher. Il m’est particulièrement cher, et il l’est bien plus encore pour toi, dans la vie de tous les jours comme dans le Seigneur.
fr.R: C’est peut-être pour cela qu’Onésime a été loin de toi pendant un peu de temps : pour que tu le retrouves pour toujours. \v 16 Mais maintenant, il n’est plus seulement un esclave. Il est bien plus qu’un esclave. C’est un frère que nous aimons. Il compte beaucoup pour moi, et il devrait compter encore plus pour toi, à la fois comme membre de ta maison et comme frère dans le Seigneur.

decisions.choice: he was separated: a passive that hints at God's purpose
alternatives: he left of his own accord
decisions.reason: Paul does not say "he ran away" or "he left you". The passive leaves room for God's hand in what happened, as Joseph said of his brothers' wrong (Genesis 50:20); τάχα ("perhaps") keeps it modest.

decisions.choice: forever: for good, and for all eternity
decisions.reason: αἰώνιον is the word for "eternal", as in eternal life. Here it is set against πρὸς ὥραν ("for an hour"): Philemon lost Onesimus for a short time and gets him back for good, and as a brother in Christ the bond will outlast this life.

decisions.choice: no longer as a slave: Philemon is to receive and treat him as a brother; whether Paul asks for his legal freedom is not said
alternatives: Paul asks Philemon to free him
decisions.reason: ὡς ("as") speaks of how Philemon is to regard him. Onesimus is "more than a slave, a beloved brother", and Philemon is to welcome him as he would Paul (verse 17). Verse 21 ("you will do even more than I say") may hint at more, perhaps his freedom or his return to Paul, but the letter does not spell it out.

decisions.choice: in the flesh and in the Lord: in ordinary human life and as fellow believers
decisions.reason: "In the flesh" is everyday human relationship, here the household, as in "masters according to the flesh" (Colossians 3:22). In both spheres Onesimus is now Philemon's brother.

decisions.choice: forever (L, R); for good (B)
decisions.reason: The key term "eternal" is not used: the contrast with "for an hour" calls for "forever" (m2).

decisions.choice: Onesimus
decisions.reason: Readable names him, since this verse starts a new thought.

decisions.choice: in everyday life (B); as a person in your household (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in the flesh" means here (m4).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it in Philemon 16: the verse sets Onesimus's status as a slave, one owned, against his place as a brother (m3).

decisions.choice: esclave at every level
decisions.reason: As the English and the style guide: here slavery itself is the point, Onesimus's legal status set against his place as a brother (m3), so "serviteur" would hide it.

source.text: Εἰ οὖν με ἔχεις κοινωνόν, προσλαβοῦ αὐτὸν ὡς ἐμέ.

records.literal_gloss: If then me you have [as] partner, receive him as me.

en.L: If then you consider me a partner, receive him as [you would] me.
en.B: So if I am your partner, take him in as though he were me.
en.R: So if you think of me as your friend and partner, welcome Onesimus the way you would welcome me.

fr.L: Si donc tu me tiens pour [ton] associé, accueille-le comme moi.
fr.B: Si donc je suis ton associé, accueille-le comme si c’était moi.
fr.R: Alors, si tu me considères comme ton ami et ton associé, accueille Onésime comme tu m’accueillerais moi-même.

decisions.choice: partner: one who shares in a common life and work
decisions.reason: κοινωνόν belongs with "sharing" in verse 6: Paul and Philemon are partners in Christ, so Philemon should treat Onesimus as he would treat Paul.

decisions.choice: receive: welcome into one's home and fellowship
decisions.reason: προσλαμβάνομαι is the word for receiving someone as one's own (Romans 15:7).

decisions.choice: Onesimus
decisions.reason: Readable names him for clarity.

decisions.choice: associé
decisions.reason: The word is one who shares a common life and work (m1); "associé" keeps the sense of a shared undertaking and fits the business words of the next verse, where "compagnon" would be only friendship.

source.text: εἰ δέ τι ἠδίκησέν σε ἢ ὀφείλει, τοῦτο ἐμοὶ ἐλλόγα·

records.literal_gloss: If but anything he wronged you or owes, this to me charge;

en.L: And if he has wronged you in anything or owes [you anything], charge this to me.
en.B: If he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, put it on my account.
en.R: If he has done anything wrong to you, or if he owes you anything, I will pay for it. Just put it on my bill.

fr.L: Et s’il t’a fait quelque tort ou [te] doit [quelque chose], porte cela à mon compte.
fr.B: S’il t’a causé du tort, ou s’il te doit quoi que ce soit, mets-le sur mon compte.
fr.R: S’il t’a fait du tort, ou s’il te doit quelque chose, je te le paierai. Tu n’as qu’à le mettre sur ma note.

decisions.choice: the wrong: some loss Onesimus caused Philemon, which the letter does not explain
decisions.reason: The letter does not say how Onesimus came to be with Paul. Many have thought he ran away, perhaps taking money with him, which Roman law punished severely; others think he went to Paul, his master's friend, to ask him to plead for him after a quarrel. Paul's "if" speaks of the matter tactfully.

decisions.choice: charge to my account: a business word
decisions.reason: ἐλλογέω means to enter something in an account (Romans 5:13). Paul takes Onesimus's debt as his own.

decisions.choice: I will pay for it. Just put it on my bill.
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the business term means (m2).

source.text: ἐγὼ Παῦλος ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί, ἐγὼ ἀποτίσω· ἵνα μὴ λέγω σοι ὅτι καὶ σεαυτόν μοι προσοφείλεις.

records.literal_gloss: I Paul wrote with the my hand, I will repay; so that not I say to you that even yourself to me you owe besides.

en.L: I, Paul, am writing [this] with my own hand: I will repay [it], not to mention to you that you owe me even your own self.
en.B: I, Paul, write this in my own hand: I will repay it. I need not remind you that you owe me your own self as well.
en.R: I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I will pay it back. Of course, I will not talk about how much you owe me. You owe me your very life!

fr.L: Moi, Paul, j’écris [ceci] de ma propre main : moi, je paierai, pour ne pas te dire que tu me dois en plus ta propre personne.
fr.B: Moi, Paul, je l’écris de ma propre main : je te rembourserai. Je n’ai pas besoin de te rappeler que tu me dois aussi ta propre personne.
fr.R: Moi, Paul, je l’écris de ma propre main : je te le rembourserai. Bien sûr, je ne parlerai pas de tout ce que tu me dois. Tu me dois ta vie même !

decisions.choice: written in Paul's own hand: like a signed promise to pay
decisions.reason: A debtor wrote out and signed his own note of debt (compare the "handwritten bond" of Colossians 2:14). Paul either took the pen at this point, as in Colossians 4:18, or wrote the whole letter himself. ἔγραψα is the past tense of letters: "I write".

decisions.choice: not to mention: a way of mentioning it
decisions.reason: Paul says he will not say it, and so says it: Philemon owes Paul his very self, because he came to faith through Paul. προσοφείλω means to owe in addition, or in return.

decisions.choice: your very life
decisions.reason: Readable says what Philemon owes: his new life in Christ (m2).

source.text: ναί, ἀδελφέ, ἐγώ σου ὀναίμην ἐν κυρίῳ· ἀνάπαυσόν μου τὰ σπλάγχνα ἐν Χριστῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Yes, brother, I of you may have benefit in [the] Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.

en.L: Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in [the] Lord; refresh my heart in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Yes, my brother, I would like you to do me this favor in the Lord. Cheer my heart as one who belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Oui, frère, que je tire de toi quelque profit dans le Seigneur ; soulage mon cœur {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}.
fr.B: Oui, frère, accorde-moi ce bienfait dans le Seigneur. Réconforte mon cœur {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}.
fr.R: Oui, mon frère, j’aimerais que tu me fasses cette faveur, dans le Seigneur. Réjouis mon cœur, toi qui appartiens au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: let me have benefit from you: another play on the name Onesimus
decisions.reason: ὀνίνημι ("to have benefit") is from the same root as the name Onesimus (see verse 11). Paul asks Philemon to be "useful" to him by welcoming Onesimus.

decisions.choice: refresh my heart: what Philemon has done for others
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 7, where Philemon refreshed the hearts of God's people; Paul asks him to do the same for him, in the way he receives Onesimus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: Cheer my heart
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words, as in verse 7.

source.text: πεποιθὼς τῇ ὑπακοῇ σου ἔγραψά σοι, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑπὲρ ἃ λέγω ποιήσεις.

records.literal_gloss: Having been persuaded of the obedience of you I wrote to you, knowing that even beyond what I say you will do.

en.L: Being confident in your obedience I wrote to you, knowing that you will do even beyond what I say.
en.B: I write to you sure that you will do what I ask, and I know you will do even more than I say.
en.R: I am sure you will do what I ask. That is why I am writing to you. I know you will do even more than I ask.

fr.L: Confiant en ton obéissance, je t’ai écrit, sachant que tu feras même au-delà de ce que je dis.
fr.B: Je t’écris, certain que tu feras ce que je demande, et je sais que tu feras même plus que je ne dis.
fr.R: Je suis sûr que tu feras ce que je te demande. C’est pour cela que je t’écris. Je sais que tu feras même plus que ce que je demande.

decisions.choice: obedience: Philemon's readiness to do what the Lord asks through Paul
decisions.reason: Paul has chosen to appeal rather than command (verse 8), yet he trusts that Philemon will obey, in the end to Christ.

decisions.choice: even more than I say: Paul does not say what
decisions.reason: Some see a hint that Philemon should free Onesimus, or send him back to help Paul (verse 13). The letter leaves it to Philemon.

decisions.choice: I write (B); I am writing (R)
decisions.reason: The past tense of letters (as in verse 19).

source.text: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἑτοίμαζέ μοι ξενίαν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ ὅτι διὰ τῶν προσευχῶν ὑμῶν χαρισθήσομαι ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: At the same time and also prepare for me a guest room, I hope for that through the prayers of you I will be granted to you.

en.L: And at the same time also prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be granted to you.
en.B: Meanwhile, please also have a room ready for me, for I hope that God will answer your prayers and give me back to you.
en.R: Also, please get a room ready for me. I hope that God will answer your prayers and let me come to visit you.

fr.L: Et en même temps, prépare-moi aussi un logement, car j’espère que, grâce à vos prières, je vous serai accordé.
fr.B: En attendant, prépare-moi aussi une chambre, car j’espère que Dieu répondra à vos prières et me rendra à vous.
fr.R: Prépare-moi aussi une chambre, s’il te plaît. J’espère que Dieu répondra à vos prières et me permettra de venir vous voir.

decisions.choice: your prayers ... granted to you: plural, the whole church
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν and ὑμῖν are plural: the church in Philemon's house has been praying for Paul's release.

decisions.choice: granted: given as a gift, freed by God in answer to prayer
decisions.reason: χαρίζομαι is related to the word for grace: to give freely (Acts 27:24). Paul hopes God will release him. His coming visit is also a gentle reminder that he will see how Onesimus has been received.

decisions.choice: a guest room: lodging for a visitor
decisions.reason: ξενίαν is hospitality, or the room a guest stays in.

decisions.choice: God will answer your prayers and give me back to you (B); God will answer your prayers and let me come to visit you (R)
alternatives: through your prayers I will be granted to you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver (m2).

source.text: Ἀσπάζεταί σε Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, Μᾶρκος, Ἀρίσταρχος, Δημᾶς, Λουκᾶς, οἱ συνεργοί μου.

records.literal_gloss: Greets you Epaphras the fellow prisoner of me in Christ Jesus, \v 24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, the fellow workers of me.

en.L: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, greets you, \v 24 [as do] Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.
en.B: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, sends you greetings, \v 24 and so do my fellow workers Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke.
en.R: Epaphras says hello. He is in prison with me because of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke also say hello. They work with me.

fr.L: Épaphras, mon compagnon de captivité {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, te salue, \v 24 [ainsi que] Marc, Aristarque, Démas, Luc, mes collaborateurs.
fr.B: Épaphras, mon compagnon de captivité {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, te salue, \v 24 ainsi que mes collaborateurs Marc, Aristarque, Démas et Luc.
fr.R: Épaphras te salue. Il est en prison avec moi à cause du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. \v 24 Marc, Aristarque, Démas et Luc te saluent aussi. Ils travaillent avec moi.

decisions.choice: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner
decisions.reason: Epaphras was a Colossian who brought the gospel there (Colossians 1:7; 4:12). Here he shares Paul's imprisonment; in Colossians 4:10 the same word is used of Aristarchus. They may have taken turns sharing Paul's custody, or the word may be meant in a wider sense.

decisions.choice: the same names as in Colossians
decisions.reason: Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke all send greetings in Colossians 4:10-14, with Epaphras. The two letters were most likely written at the same time and carried together (Colossians 4:7-9).

decisions.choice: you: singular, Philemon
decisions.reason: The greetings are sent to Philemon himself.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: He is in prison with me because of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
alternatives: my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what "fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus" means.

source.text: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ [be] with the spirit of you.

en.L: The grace of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [be] with your spirit.
en.B: May the grace of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with your spirit.
en.R: May the grace of the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be with all of you, deep in your spirit.

fr.L: La grâce du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} [soit] avec votre esprit.
fr.B: Que la grâce du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} soit avec votre esprit.
fr.R: Que la grâce du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} soit avec vous tous, au plus profond de votre esprit.

decisions.choice: your: plural, the whole church
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν is plural: the closing blessing is for everyone who hears the letter.

decisions.choice: your spirit: you yourselves, in your inmost being
decisions.reason: The same blessing closes Philippians (4:23) and Galatians (6:18).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: all of you
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "your" is plural here (m1), as Philippians 4:23 does.
